ADVERSE FACT KEPT ON THE RECORD FOR CONFLICT 1: the WHO Joint External Evaluation mission (metadata index 20) was physically in Asmara 3-8 OCTOBER 2016, between the Arbi Harnet dispatches of 25 September and 27 October, and produced no trace of the outbreak - cholera appears once, generically ('the MoH has previous experience in requesting support for cholera, H1N1 and polio outbreaks'). FOR THE MODELLERS - THE HEADLINE POINT. BMJ Global Health 2025 (index 32, verified by me via Europe PMC fullTextXML) places Eritrea in the WASH cluster with the lowest service access, highest open defaecation and highest surface-water drinking, alongside Burundi, CAR, Chad, DRC, Ethiopia, Madagascar, Niger, South Sudan and Tanzania, and finds 'Areas with insufficient WASH are the same with high burden cholera outbreaks.' Every other member of that cluster carries a large recorded burden; Eritrea's recorded 120 cases over 2000-2023 is a gross outlier against its own risk profile by WHO AFRO's own analysis. Eritrea's near-empty series is an ASCERTAINMENT ARTEFACT, not low transmission.
